definition: Forward masking is an auditory testing approach in which an earlier sound makes a later, low-level sound harder or just impossible to hear. It is used in temporal masking curve methods to study cochlear or basilar-membrane input-output characteristics and aspects of hearing loss beyond simple tone-detection thresholds.

reasons: The definition’s first sentence (“in which an earlier sound makes a later, low-level sound harder or just impossible to hear”) is not stated in the provided packet text.

The definition describes forward masking as “used in temporal masking curve methods”; while the packet mentions “forward masking experiments” and separately discusses “temporal masking curve (TMC) paradigm,” it does not explicitly support that forward masking is used “in” TMC methods as characterized in the definition.

The definition’s mention of studying “cochlear or basilar-membrane input-output characteristics and aspects of hearing loss beyond simple tone-detection thresholds” is only partially supported: the packet supports the basilar-membrane input-output and beyond pure-tone audiometry motivation, but does not explicitly connect cochlear input-output in the specific way asserted.
